title: Drum solos and featuring in early bands
summary: The Piron-era bands did not feature drum solos; showy drumming belonged to theatre pits and featuring began in recent years.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Tell me, in all these bands, like the Pierron band and things like that, did they ever have drum solos? Hmm? Did they ever have drum solos in any of these bands?

No, we didn't use that style. They were just, you know, straight to the good jet playing, you know, playing. Mostly rhythms, you know. They didn't use all this feature and stuff like we use now, you know.
When was the first time they started using featuring?
Well, yeah, just recently, say about ten, twelve years ago they started that, yeah. When these clubs and things started, you know, they started using the band as a show, as dance music, you know.
Tell me, Black Happy used to play drum solos down at the Lyric Theatre.
No, no, not Black Happy. There was another club. Oh, Red Happy. Red Happy, yeah. He played the, yeah. He played drum solos down there?
Well yeah, in the theatre jet they used that, you know. They had another boy came here from Texas.

He used to juggle the sticks, you know, and all that sort of stuff, you know. Eccentric, you know. Well in the show pit, you know, in the theatre pit they'd do those things, but not dance work, you know.
